title: Properties of solids and plane shapes
canonical_examples_source: Arithmetic self-verified; method ref: NCERT Class 5/6 Maths; format ref: bank uk-ks2-2024 maths.

blocks.content: Shapes are all around us. Flat shapes are called plane shapes; solid shapes take up space. Each has properties we can count and name. Quick words: plane shape means a flat drawing like a square or circle that has no thickness.
A solid has faces (flat surfaces), edges (where faces meet) and vertices (corners). A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices.

steps: The edges meet at 8 corners, called vertices.

blocks.explain: A cube has 6 flat square faces.
blocks.rule: A solid's faces are its flat surfaces, edges are where faces meet, vertices are the corners.

blocks.content: A plane shape is flat. Name it by counting its straight sides: 3 is a triangle, 4 a quadrilateral, 5 a pentagon.

blocks.explain: A pentagon is a plane shape with 5 straight sides.
blocks.rule: Count the straight sides to name a plane shape.

blocks.question: Sara says a cube and a square are the same shape. Why is that not right?
options: A cube is a 3D solid with 6 square faces; a square is one flat 2D shape
blocks.explain: A square is flat — it has length and width only (2D). A cube is a solid you can hold — it has length, width and height (3D), and it is made of 6 square faces. A square is just one of those faces.
blocks.rule: Solids are 3D (faces, edges, vertices); plane shapes are flat 2D.
blocks.principle: A flat face of a solid is not the same as the whole solid.
canonical_solution: A square is a flat 2D shape
So a square is one face of a cube, not the cube itself

rubric.look_for: notes a cube has 6 square faces
explains a face is not the whole solid

misconceptions.if: treats square and cube as identical
misconceptions.coach: A square is flat; a cube is solid with 6 square faces.
Count them: a cube has 6 faces.
